title: Read and Choose
aim: Read the drop, the paddle and the player across from you, and pick the shot that fits: attack it, reset it, or place it.

stages.title: Air or Step Back
stages.inShort: A drops from the baseline, and B takes it out of the air or steps back and hits it at the top of the bounce.
rules: A starts at the baseline, B at the kitchen line. A plays drops (soft balls that land in or near the kitchen): some low and good, some high and easy to attack.
B always tries first to take the ball out of the air, reaching in with a roll volley (a volley with a short brushing upward swing).
Can't reach it in the air? Step back, open the outside foot, let it bounce and hit it at the top of the bounce with a compact topspin swing.
No half-volleys (hitting the ball just after it bounces, down at your feet). If B gets caught with one, the point goes to A.
stages.tooEasy: A mixes good and weak drops on purpose, changes the depth, and makes the drops deeper and with more spin, so B has less time.
stages.tooHard: A calls each drop as it goes: "good" or "weak".
stages.goodLooksLike: B decides early, air or step back, and never ends up stuck with a half-volley.

stages.title: Read the Paddle
stages.inShort: A shows the paddle high, middle or low before each shot, and B gets ready for what is coming.
rules: A stands at the kitchen line, B in the middle of the court (between baseline and kitchen line).
Before each shot, A clearly shows the paddle: high, middle or low. A mixes forehand and backhand.
Paddle high: B lowers the paddle and gets ready to reset (a soft ball that takes the pace off and drops low).
Paddle low: B gets into an attacking stance, ready to step forward.
Paddle middle: B split-steps (a small hop that lands just as A hits) and decides after A has hit.
stages.tooEasy: A hides the paddle and mixes freely, so B has to read it. B may only counter (hit back hard) when B read the paddle right.
stages.tooHard: A also calls the position out loud before hitting: "high", "middle" or "low".
stages.goodLooksLike: B always takes a step in the right direction before the ball arrives.

stages.title: Wide or Middle
stages.inShort: A plays a fixed style, and B picks where to dink to match it: half wide against an aggressive A, mostly wide against a passive A.
rules: A and B dink cross-court (diagonal) at the kitchen line. B places the dinks. A plays a fixed style for each round.
Round 1, A plays aggressive: takes every ball out of the air. B dinks about half wide, half to the middle, mixed, not strictly in turn.
Round 2, A plays passive: lets every ball bounce, steady. B dinks mostly wide, now and then to the middle or down the line.
Before each round B says the split out loud: "half and half" or "mostly wide". No points.
Pulled wide: B takes a drop step (a step back that makes room) and gets back toward the middle.
B attacks only a pop-up (a ball that bounces up high), and only when balanced. Never speed up off-balance.
stages.tooEasy: Play for points: a pop-up B puts away scores. Harder still: A switches style at random each rally, and B reads it and changes the split live.
stages.tooHard: Stay longer in one round with the same style, until B's split feels automatic.
stages.goodLooksLike: A pop-up comes, and B puts it away from a balanced stance.
